description: A line producer must approve the binding capture and presentation package for a one-night City Arts Gala being recorded in a historic theater, including the camera configuration, archive permissions, headliner production plan, sponsor treatment, and accessibility setup.

shared_context.S1: The City Arts Gala will take place in the 900-seat Orpheum Theater and will be recorded for the gala broadcast.
shared_context.S2: The current draft package uses three cameras, permits the recording to be reused in the festival archive, includes a sponsor product display on stage, and plans a general caption feed.
shared_context.S3: The gala is scheduled for Saturday evening, with the headliner currently listed for the final performance.
shared_context.S4: Mara makes the binding production approval after the normal pre-lock round-robin in which technical, rights, talent, and accessibility leads report their final operating requirements.

PF1.text: Devon's completed radio-frequency survey found that wireless roaming camera links interfere with the theater's assistive-listening loop; the gala must use three fixed wired cameras from the marked camera platforms. Devon filed the survey in the technical folder but it is not on Mara's draft lock sheet.

PF2.text: Leila's signed performance license permits the gala broadcast but prohibits any video-on-demand release or later promotional clips; the recording must be marked broadcast-only. Leila received the countersigned license this morning and has not yet entered the restriction in the rights tracker.

PF3.text: Jonah confirmed with the headliner's agent that the performer can soundcheck only at exactly 3:00 PM and that the rider prohibits sponsor product placement anywhere on the performance stage. Jonah has the agent's confirmation in email but it is not in the production schedule.

PF4.text: Nia's accessibility vendor confirmed that the live caption feed requires the captioner to work from Booth B, whose dedicated return feed is connected to the gala's caption encoder; the general plan's control-room location will not work. Nia documented the vendor confirmation in the accessibility file but has not added the booth assignment to the lock sheet.

acceptance_conditions: The gala must use three fixed wired cameras from the marked platforms.
The recording must be restricted to the gala broadcast and not released on demand or as later promotional clips.
The headliner soundcheck must be scheduled for exactly 3:00 PM.
No sponsor product may be placed on the performance stage.
The live captioner must be assigned to Booth B.
The final package must log the technical, rights, talent, and accessibility changes as commitments.

content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] == 'technical_lock_update' for c in commitments) and any(c['type'] == 'rights_holdback' for c in commitments) and any(c['type'] == 'talent_schedule_update' for c in commitments) and any(c['type'] == 'sponsor_removal' for c in commitments) and any(c['type'] == 'captioning_assignment' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The radio-frequency survey changes the camera choice from the draft's unspecified three-camera plan to exactly three fixed wired cameras and requires the technical lock update.
The signed license changes archive reuse from permitted to broadcast-only, requires the rights holdback, and supplies the specific private fact Mara must cite.
The agent confirmation changes the soundcheck to exactly 3:00 PM and removes the draft stage product display, requiring both the talent schedule update and sponsor removal.
The vendor's encoder confirmation changes the captioner assignment from the generic control-room plan to exactly Booth B and requires the captioning assignment.
